Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=tests/fixtures/handoff_exit.S lines=whole file kind=dead-file
Claim: Legacy fixture (per the Makefile's own note) whose ELF is consumed only by vsim's handoff_smoke.cpp -- an EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL manual binary never registered with CTest -- yet it is still built by the default 'all' target and the 'dump' target.
Evidence given: tests/fixtures/Makefile:96-98: 'handoff_exit.elf... are legacy (referenced only by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp)... not in active CTest'. Only cross-repo reference: vsim tests/hybrid/handoff_smoke.cpp, built EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL under VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID (vsim CMakeLists.txt:527-530) and absent from cmake/HybridConfig.cmake test registrations. No andesim test script or runner references handoff_exit. Built in 'all' (Makefile:89) and 'dump' (Makefile:189-191).

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	// vsim resumes at _start, sets a2=3, retires slti x0, x0,  0x5A1 to trigger the
2	// vsim->QEMU handoff (drain state, exit 200). The infinite spin is a
3	// safety net if the trigger is missed.
4	
5	.section .text
6	.globl _start
7	_start:
8	    li      a2, 3
9	    slti   x0, x0,  0x5A1
10	1:  j       1b
11

1	# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
2	#
3	# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
4	# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
5	# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
6	# to bypass the env var.
7	
8	TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
9	# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
10	# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
11	# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
12	rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
13	CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
14	LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
15	OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
16	
17	# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
18	# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
19	# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
20	RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
21	LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
22	# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
23	HELPERS_DIR := runtime
24	
25	CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
26	LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static
27	
28	# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
29	RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
30	               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
31	               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
32	               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
33	
34	# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
35	# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
36	# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
37	BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
38	                  break_verify_diverge
39	
40	# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
41	# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
42	# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
43	# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
44	# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
45	# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
46	# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
47	# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
48	# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
49	# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
50	RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
51	                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
52	RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
53	                    rt_c_hvm_data
54	RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file
55	
56	RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
57	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
58	# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
59	RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
60	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
61	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
62	VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
63	VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
64	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
65	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
66	VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
67	# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
68	# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
69	# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
70	VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
71	
72	# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
73	# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
74	# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
75	# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
76	# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
77	TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
78	CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
79	LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
80	CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
81	VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
82	VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
83	VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
84	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
85	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
86	
87	.PHONY: all clean dump rv32
88	
89	all: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
90	     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
91	     hvm_readback.elf \
92	     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
93	     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
94	     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
95	
96	# Note: handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are legacy (referenced only
97	# by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp). They still build for completeness
98	# but are not in active CTest. All targets now share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.
99	
100	spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
101		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
102		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
103	
104	handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
105		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
106		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@
107	
108	handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
109		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
110		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
111	
112	# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
113	# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
114	# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
115	# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
116	l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
117		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
118		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
119	lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
120	
121	# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
122	# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
123	# the exit code).
124	lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
125	                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
126		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
127	
128	# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
129	# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
130	hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
131		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
132	
133	$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
134		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
135		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
136	
137	# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
138	# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
139	$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
140		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
141		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
142	
143	# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
144	# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
145	$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
146		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
147		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
148	
149	# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
150	# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
151	$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
152		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
153		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
154	rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
155	
156	# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
157	# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
158	$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
159		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
160	
161	# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
162	$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
163		$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)
164	
165	# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
166	# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
167	# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
168	# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
169	# same GEMM kernel.
170	rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
171		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
172		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 8 13:01:33 2026 +0800

    feat(plugin): ROI markers become RISC-V HINT NOPs; triggers are marker|pc
    
    Swap the magic-CSR ROI markers for the RISC-V HINT pair slti x0, x0, 0x5A0
    (enter) / 0x5A1 (exit): rd=x0 discards the result, so each marker is an
    architectural NOP on every conforming core. One marked ELF now runs
    standalone on fast and cycle and on real silicon, and drives --trigger
    marker on hybrid, without the old csrwi 0x7C0 hazard where CSR 0x7C0 is
    MILMB on Andes cores. This single-slice commit carries the whole rename:
    the in-tree include/hybrid/insn_match.h + handoff_site.h move to the HINT
    encoding, the plugin drops all csrwi 0x7C0 trigger wording for marker
    wording, and every .S/.c fixture marker macro plus the tests/e2e.sh MODE
    name become marker instead of csr. The in-tree headers are byte-identical
    to the v2 ABI pin, which already carries this encoding, so the next commit
    can replace them with the abi submodule with no tree change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    feat(hybrid): HandoffController exit-drain dispatch, minimal (marker EXIT + exit code)

    the StateDrain, returning the populated hybrid_state_v1; the simulator then
